extracted.intended_audience: researchers, preprint-curation groups, and readers seeking expert-evaluated preprints
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluating, curating, and summarising preprints for discovery by the research community—highlighting important/new studies, noting strengths and limitations, and organising lists of curated preprints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluated by experts / trusted experts
rubrics_metrics.description: “The latest research, evaluated by experts” / “alongside evaluations from trusted experts.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sciety assembles groups of researchers who evaluate and curate preprints; credibility of evaluations comes from being produced by expert groups and participating evaluators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discovering and highlighting important new studies (impact)
rubrics_metrics.description: “Join the global network discovering and highlighting important new studies.” / “Discover the next advancement in your field.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Curated items should be those judged important or impactful in their field—items worth highlighting and recommending to peers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relevance and findability
rubrics_metrics.description: “Search and sort through the vast preprint literature and find relevant and impactful studies in your area of expertise.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluations/curation should make it easy for readers to find studies relevant to their interests (metadata, tags, clear descriptions) so lists and search results surface appropriate work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Curation / organisation / shareability
rubrics_metrics.description: “Organise and share what you are reading. Create lists of the preprints you find interesting that you can return to in the future or share with your research community.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Curators should provide organised lists and sharing mechanisms; curation includes selecting, grouping, and summarising preprints for reuse by communities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty / significance (pioneering / landmark)
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples use language such as “elegant and pioneering technique,” “This landmark work … represents the most significant breakthrough …”.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluators should comment on novelty and whether the work represents a pioneering advance or landmark contribution to its field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical quality / methodological rigor
rubrics_metrics.description: Example notes “The technical quality of the work is exceptional, setting the bar appropriately high.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess and report on technical execution and methodological standards; high technical quality is a reason to curate and recommend a preprint.

rubrics_metrics.name: Validation / evidence supporting claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Example: “Recordings of Kir1.1, TRPM8, and TRPV1 channels are used to validate the effectiveness of the technique.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluations should note whether authors have validated methods/claims appropriately (controls, replication, direct demonstrations) and highlight evidence that supports conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency about limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Example: “A limitation is that, in its current form, the technique can be used only on melanosome-containing Xenopus oocyte membranes.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Curations should explicitly state important limitations or constraints of the study, so readers can judge generalisability and caveats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity and insightfulness of interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: Example: “Their work reveals with outstanding clarity how nascent transmembrane segments can pass…” and “Peer review added more to the conclusion and future perspectives.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluators should comment on how clearly the study communicates mechanisms/insights and whether interpretation advances understanding or suggests future directions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value as a resource / data utility
rubrics_metrics.description: Example: “The data hopefully providing a valuable resource and foundation for a better understanding of the ecology and evolution of sea urchins.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the data/products of the study constitute a usable resource for the community (e.g., genomes, datasets, methods) and their potential downstream value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality of the curated summary
rubrics_metrics.description: Curation examples succinctly summarise approach, key findings, validation, limitations, and significance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good curation text should briefly describe what was done, why it matters, key validations/limitations, and a clear take-away to help readers decide whether to read the full preprint.
